questions.q: When you describe work as trigger, steps and output, where does the lesson say AI opportunities usually sit?
options: In the trigger, such as the email or form that starts the work
In the output, such as the booked call or the polite no
In the steps that involve reading, writing, sorting or remembering
In the handoffs between the different software tools you use
questions.explain: The lesson says AI opportunities usually sit in the steps, especially those that involve reading, writing, summarizing, sorting or remembering to do something.

questions.q: At a small dental office, the receptionist handles about 90 appointment requests a month, spending about 4 minutes on each. What goes in the inventory's Hours per month column?
questions.explain: The lesson defines hours per month as frequency × minutes ÷ 60, so 90 × 4 ÷ 60 gives 6 hours.

questions.q: The owner of a 12-person print shop is about to interview staff about their recurring work. What does the lesson say to make clear at the start?
options: That answers will be used to review each person's performance
That AI will soon take over the tasks they mention most often
That only tasks with exact, measured times will be counted
That the goal is removing drudgery, not replacing people
questions.explain: The lesson says to state clearly that this is about removing drudgery, not replacing people, because fear produces polite, useless answers and honesty produces the best opportunities.
